$comment: The `hooks.guard` section is READ AT RUNTIME by src/hooks.ts and enforced by this
plugin's own `tool.execute.before`, which refuses the listed commands for sessions the
plugin spawned - the lets implementer, the one model here holding edit and bash.
It does not apply to your own session on the same server.
Set enabled=false to turn the gate off without deleting the policy that documents it.
Each `refuse` entry is a regex source plus the reason the worker is told; an entry that
does not compile is skipped rather than taking the others down with it.
Design and the measurements behind it:
`event` names the Claude Code hook phase this guard is equivalent to. ECC's OpenCode
adapter maps PreToolUse -> tool.execute.before, which is the event this plugin
registers, so a reader coming from either toolchain finds the same policy under the

refuse.reason: narrowing the test run hides failures the full suite would have caught. Run the whole suite; if a test is wrong, say so.
repointing core.hooksPath disables this repo's git hooks for every later command in the worktree.

$schema-note: Keys outside `hooks.guard` are ignored by this plugin and left for Claude Code / ECC tooling that reads the same file.
